problem: Graph-convolution object-relation modules (ORG, HOZ) implicitly learn adjacency from bounding box size and confidence, so agents over-attend to large, clear objects and ignore small or blurry but target-relevant ones (object attention bias).
motivation: Objects differ in visibility, so a GCN learns a biased adjacency matrix; e.g. attention differs by more than tenfold between the most and least attended objects. The observation is that object attention should be decoupled from object features and learned explicitly per target, so that small and ambiguous objects can still guide the search.
key_idea: Learn an explicit target-conditioned directed object attention graph (a learnable intrinsic graph plus a view-adaptive graph) and use it to reweight object features and to guide attention over image features, with a 3-parameter branch energy scaling before the LSTM.
insight: The ablations show that the intrinsic prior graph carries most of the benefit: IG alone raises SR from 70.77 to 73.67, while VAG alone without IG drops SR to 67.43, so fully adaptive learning needs a prior. The learned weights confirm this: intrinsic 0.95 vs adaptive 0.05. Adding branch-identity embeddings (BS) to the cross-attention model makes it collapse (SR 67.82), whereas 3 scalar coefficients (ED) help (74.32), so simple, low-parameter choices matter in coupled RL models. A directed graph beats an undirected one (73.15 vs 74.32 SR), and removing GCN/zone/room branches leaves performance unchanged while cutting episode time by 27%.
method: DOA graph: the object attention for target p is G_t = G_n^p·w_n + G_v·w_v, a weighted sum of an intrinsic graph and a view-adaptive graph; edges are directed from in-view objects to the target
Intrinsic graph G_n: a learnable N×N matrix (N=22) trained by RL, row-softmax normalised, fixed at test time

View adaptive graph G_v: multi-head score between a query (avg-pooled ResNet18 image feature concatenated with the target one-hot embedding OI) and confidence-filtered object features (518-d from Faster-RCNN), giving N×1 weights
UAOA: object features are mapped to 64-d via two FC layers and multiplied by the per-object attention G_t^q
UAIA: attention-aware object semantics D = Σ 1(conf>0.6)·G_t^q·OI^q act as the query in 4-head cross-attention over image features (keys/values, 1D pixel index embedding added)
ABED: three learnable scalars r1,r2,r3 scale the object, image and previous-action branches before concatenation and a pointwise conv, giving branch identity with 3 parameters

Simplified baseline plus A3C: drop the GCN, zone and room branches, keeping image, object and previous-action branches; an LSTM policy trained with A3C; Done probability boosted by detector confidence

setting.backbone: ResNet18 (image features) + Faster-RCNN (object detector, fine-tuned) + attention modules + LSTM, trained with A3C from scratch
setting.training_data: AI2-THOR: 20 rooms per scene type for training (4 types), trained for 3M episodes; Faster-RCNN fine-tuned on 50% of the training data; no extra data
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB from a single view plus target object name
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MoveAhead, RotateLeft, RotateRight, LookDown, LookUp, Done
setting.privileged: none (a ground-truth detector was only tested in an ablation)

numbers.extra: 3-run average; also reports L>=5 subset of targets: SR 67.88, SPL 40.36, SAE 32.56

numbers_note: Results are on the AI2-THOR (ALL targets) and RoboTHOR custom splits with SAE; they are not the standard RoboTHOR challenge benchmark. Values are averages of 3 test runs.
results: On AI2-THOR, DOA+ABED reaches SR 74.32 / SPL 40.27 / SAE 29.79, beating HOZ (68.53/37.50/25.98), which is the +7.4%/+8.1%/+17.6% claimed in the abstract, and beating the simplified baseline by 5.18 SR. On RoboTHOR it reaches SR 36.22 vs HOZ 31.67.
limitations: Evaluated only on AI2-THOR and RoboTHOR with 22 object categories and a fine-tuned detector; no real-robot or large-scale benchmark (e.g. HM3D)

Only the endogenous cause of bias is addressed; the long-tailed object frequency (exogenous cause) is left untouched, and the view-adaptive graph collapses to nearly one-hot attention with a weight of only 0.05
Performance depends on detector quality (GT detector gives SPL 59.12) and on the choice of backbone, with ResNet50/101 hurting SPL
